title: 戦略会計応用
subtitle: Management Accounting Advanced
keywords: Sales mix 2.Differential cost revenue analysis 3.Special cost survey 4.Net present value method 5.Internal rate of return method
educationalGoal: This course corresponds to the “Financial Ability” learning and educational goal of the Department of Management Systems. The goal is to cultivate in students the ability to properly use accounting information for business and structural decisions made by corporate managers.
advice: In corporate activities, decision-making is required in a variety of situations. In the first half of this course, students will learn how to make decisions in their daily work; in the second half of the course, students will learn how to make long-term decisions such as those involving capital investment.
books: Textbook: Not specified Reference book: Not specified Reserved Book: Not specified
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge and skills in areas such as variable income statements, CVP analysis, and DCF are required. Students should review what they learned in Basic Accounting and other accounting/finance-related courses prior to taking this class.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the sales mix and determine the optimal sales mix for multiple products.
Be able to understand the concept of differential cost revenue analysis.
Be able to understand capital procurement methods and the cost of capital.
Be able to understand the net present value method and the internal rate of return method.
Be able to understand the present value of cash flow and calculate it using specific examples.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) Be able to understand the concept of sales mix and determine the optimal sales mix under multiple conditions. 2) Be able to address complex business decision-making problems using differential cost earnings analysis. 3) Be able to use various methods to compare capital investment alternatives, including the net present value method and the internal rate of return method.
achievementLevels.standard: 1) Be able to understand the concept of sales mix and solve simple exercises. 2) Be able to address business decision-making problems using differential cost earnings analysis. 3) Be able to use the present value of cash flow in considering decision-making issues related to capital investment.
